chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Hanan ibn Sadir, who said:

I was with Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) when a man entered, said Salam, and sat down. Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asked him, 'From which country are you?' The man said, 'I am from the people of Kufah, and I am a lover and follower of yours.' He said, 'Do you establish all of your prayers in the Mosque of Kufah?' The man said, 'No.' He said, 'Verily you are deprived of the good.'

Then Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) asked, 'Do you perform a Ghusl once a day with the water of your Euphrates?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'What about once a week?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'What about once a month?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'What about once a year?' He said, 'No.' He said to him, 'Verily you are deprived of the good.'

Then he asked, 'Do you visit the grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) once a week?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'What about once a month?' He said, 'No.' He said, 'What about once a year?' He said, 'No.' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said, 'Verily you are deprived of the good.'

key_terms.قَبْرُ الْحُسَيْنِ (ع): Grave of al-Husayn (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Baqir teach about the importance of consistent prayer and Ziyarah in Kufah?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Baqir (AS) engages a Kufan devotee to illustrate that mere affection (*mawala*) is insufficient without consistent ritual action (*amal*). By systematically questioning the man's neglect of daily Ghusl from the Euphrates, regular prayer in Kufah, and frequent Ziyarah to Imam al-Husayn (AS), the Imam emphasizes that these acts are vital channels for receiving divine bounty (*khayr*), a core theme in Shia devotional practice.
